items.stem: In a multistage dividend discount model, the terminal value is most sensitive to which assumption?

options.text: The long-run (terminal) growth rate relative to the discount rate
options.rationale: Correct: terminal value hinges on the gap between the discount rate and terminal growth.

options.text: The dividend paid in year one only
options.rationale: A single near-term dividend has small effect on terminal value.

options.text: The number of decimal places used
options.rationale: Rounding precision is immaterial to sensitivity.
The ticker has no bearing on valuation.

items.explanation: Correct: terminal value hinges on the gap between the discount rate and terminal growth.

items.stem: An analyst accepts a lavish gift from a client that could affect objectivity. Under the Standards, the best action is to:

options.text: Disclose and obtain employer consent before accepting
options.rationale: Correct: the Standards require disclosure and consent for gifts that could impair objectivity.

options.text: Accept silently because it is customary
options.rationale: Non-disclosure of a benefit that could impair objectivity breaches the Standards.

options.text: Accept and offset it with a donation
options.rationale: A donation does not cure the independence/objectivity concern.
An extreme refusal is not what the Standards require.

items.explanation: Correct: the Standards require disclosure and consent for gifts that could impair objectivity.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about a callable bond are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Its value is lower than an otherwise identical option-free bond
options.rationale: Correct: the embedded call benefits the issuer, reducing value to the holder.

options.text: Effective duration captures its rate sensitivity better than modified duration
options.rationale: Correct: with an embedded option, effective duration is appropriate.

options.text: It can never be redeemed before maturity
options.rationale: A call feature lets the issuer redeem early, which is the point of the option.

options.text: Its yield is always lower than a comparable option-free bond
options.rationale: Investors demand a higher yield to bear call risk, not lower.

items.explanation: Correct: the embedded call benefits the issuer, reducing value to the holder.
